final.label: buffer-lifetime-or-alignment

skill_entry.name: 14. A buffer's lifetime and alignment follow its consumer, not its declaration
skill_entry.trigger: Any one arm, each a grep over added production lines. Arm A, asynchronous release: an added line is an ownership transition of a DMA-heap buffer: allocation (`dma_allocate*`, `alloc_buffer`), release (`dma_deallocate`, `release_buffer`, `free_staging_if_idle`), submission (`xfer_blocks`, `xfer_n_blocks`, `xfer_gof(s)`), tracker push or pop, `reset()`/`abandon()` of the owning record, a destructor body, or a new owning member of a record handed to the engine (`pending_xfer`, `pinned_gof`, `pinned_batch`). Arm B, reserve literal: the diff adds `v.reserve(<number>)` on a std::vector and the same function holds a reference or pointer into `v` across `push_back`/`emplace_back`/`insert`/`resize`. Arm C, scratch to SIMD: a new `std::array<bf16|float|uint8_t|__m256i|__m512i, N>` or C array without `alignas`, whose pointer goes to `destination`/`dest`/`scratch`/`out` or a `std::function` member.
skill_entry.procedure: Arm A: per owning struct read destructor, `complete()`, `abandon()`, every holder. Write allocate -> populate -> submit -> tracker push -> completion (`poll_completions`, `hwcacheblock::wait`) -> release. List every other drop path (record destructor, `clear()`, `~dma_tracker` and whether it calls `clear()` before its queues die, `reset()`, queue out of scope); each waits, leaks on purpose (nulls `data`), or frees. A free after submission with no wait is the finding; a missing exclusivity assert is a nit inside it. Arm B: record the reserve value and what bounds the pushes; absent next to the reserve, the finding is the question. Then follow each growth call to the next read of the reference; a read reached without `continue`/`break`/`return` upgrades it to a defect (growth-call arguments are evaluated before reallocation). Arm C: resolve the consumer to one overload (match the destination pointer type; for a `std::function` member, every assignment site), grep its body for aligned intrinsics (`_mm256_*` 32 bytes, `_mm512_*` 64), compare with `alignas` or the element type's definition (bf16 = `__bf16`, 2 bytes), grep siblings in the file for `alignas`, check whether any test drives the real consumer. Runtime proof: a standalone UBSan reproducer (no tron build) or a `-S` stack offset; else `Insufficient data: not compiled`.
skill_entry.question: After the line that frees this buffer, hands it to its consumer, or could reallocate its container, who still reads it, does the declared alignment reach the consumer's widest aligned store, and what bounds the pushes past the reserve literal?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A drop path that runs only before submission (7f80aa17da:h/tron/gof.hpp:267-271). A buffer submitted and never freed (PR 1722 `hwcacheblock` blocks `new`ed into rings, no delete; APPROVED at aac65930a5). Type or parameter renames inside an owning struct (PR 3756, APPROVED at 7206e88cc2). A wait covering the wrong device set (check index-count-or-wait-set-mismatch); a readiness predicate exposing unfinished pages (concurrency check). Consumers using only unaligned forms, `memcpy`, `std::copy_n`, scalar code. Heap buffers from `dma_allocate_aligned(size, HWCACHEBLOCK_ALIGN_BYTES)` or `alloc_align`. A new aligned store through a pointer parameter with no new buffer (PR 2693 added `page::get_v` with `_mm256_store_si256`, APPROVED silently). A held reference with no literal reserve (PR 4353 `worker_plan`, author comment keeps references valid, APPROVED at a9a9cf30a4). Lifetime machinery with test rows per drop path (PR 2906, APPROVED). Intrinsic choice, kernel arithmetic, the literal inside `alignas` (check 13). Never block on this check.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Arm A: 'dropping a queued `<record>` without `<release>` frees `<buffer>` under live DMA; only `<path>` remembers today. Fix: `<release>` in the destructor unless completed, or wait for the descriptor in `<drop path>`.' Arm B: 'why <N>? perhaps a comment explaining... How deep do we get in your tests?' then, as a self-reply: 'if you do `push_back` enough times to exceed <N> and it has to reallocate, it will invalidate any references you are currently holding (`<ref>` at :<line>). Whereas, a std::deque won't... in case you think it matters.' Arm C: '`<buffer>` (<file:line>) introduces an ordinary stack array, then passes it through `<callback>` to `<consumer>`. That gather uses `<intrinsic>`, requiring <N>-byte alignment. Fix: add alignas(<CONST>), matching the <sibling> scratch, and exercise the real gather through <production path>.'
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: Arm A: 'Top robustness item' in a list he forwarded from an assistant (5498556672, issue comment; normal; the author changed teardown to wait-in-clear, not the suggested abandon-in-destructor). Arm C: a statement, the consequence, what he ran (compile, UBSan), then 'Fix:' (3960506641; normal; the author added alignas and a test at 7f80aa17da). Arm B: a question first ('why 64?', 3120756577), the mechanism as a self-reply ending 'in case you think it matters' (3120788282; nit; author kept std::vector, raised reserve to 1024, Wade APPROVED 4156364038). Never CHANGES_REQUESTED.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file (the function declaring the buffer, the reserve or the reference); other files (consumer header h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp, src/pos/dma_tracker.cpp, h/pos/config.hpp for the alignment constant, the element type's definition); callers (every assignment site of a std::function member, every holder of the record); GitHub contents API when the commented head is force-pushed away; runtime optional (standalone UBSan reproducer or `-S` stack offset), otherwise Insufficient data.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: buffer lifetime and alignment follow the consumer

Common setup additions: reuse pr.diff for the three greps. Diff greps return pr.diff line numbers; to get the HEAD line of a hit run `git -C WT grep -n -F '<matched text without the leading +>' HEAD -- <file>`, or add the hit's offset inside its hunk to the `+start` of the nearest `@@` header above it (`git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- <file>`). If HEAD is the commit next to a reviewer comment and `git -C WT cat-file -t HEAD` fails (force-pushed away), fetch each file the comment names with `gh api "repos/positron-ai/tron/contents/<path>?ref=HEAD" -q .content | base64 -d > old/<path>` and build the diff with `diff -u <(git -C WT show BASE:<path>) old/<path>`; run the greps on that file instead of pr.diff.

Arm A (asynchronous release):
1. `grep -nE '^\+[^/]*(dma_allocate|dma_deallocate|release_buffer|free_staging|abandon\(|\.pop\(\)|\.reset\(\)|xfer_(n_)?blocks\(|xfer_gofs?\(|dma_tracker::push|~[a-z_]+\(\)\s*\{)' pr.diff` (the `[^/]*` drops comment lines; `\s*\{` keeps only destructor definitions). Keep hits inside a struct that owns the pointer or a function that submits it; a hunk that only renames a parameter or member type inside such a struct does not count.
2. Per owning struct S: `git -C WT show HEAD:<header> | awk '/struct S/,/^};/'` and `git -C WT grep -n 'S' HEAD -- h src` for the destructor, `complete()`, `abandon()` and every holder. Write the sequence allocate -> populate -> submit -> push -> completion observed -> release.
3. Drop paths: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'clear\(\)|~dma_tracker|q\.pop\(\)|\.reset\(\)|std::optional<pending_xfer>' HEAD -- src/pos/dma_tracker.cpp h/pos/dma_tracker.hpp`. For each, read until the record dies and record: waits (`hwcacheblock::wait`), leaks on purpose (`abandon()` sets `data = nullptr`), or frees. For `~dma_tracker` the deciding line is whether it calls `clear()` before its queue members are destroyed; if not, queue destruction reaches the record destructor, whose outcome is the path's outcome. For the record destructor read whether the free is conditional on completion; an unconditional `if (data) dma_deallocate` is "frees". A free with no wait after submission is the finding.
4. Exclusive fields: `git -C WT show HEAD:h/pos/dma_tracker.hpp | grep -n 'pinned_'` and `git -C WT grep -n 'TRON_ASSERT.*pinned' HEAD -- src/pos/dma_tracker.cpp`; no assert that `pinned_gof` and `pinned_batch` are exclusive is a nit inside an Arm A finding, never standalone.

Arm B (reserve literal with a held reference):
5. `grep -nE '^\+.*\.reserve\([0-9]+\)' pr.diff` lists literal reserves; take the container name V from each line. For each V: `grep -nE '^\+.*&\s*[a-z_]+\s*=\s*V(\.(back|front)\(\)|\[)|= *V\.data\(\)' pr.diff` finds held references (the `\s*` after `&` is required: Wade's site is `frame_t& f = stk.back();`), and `grep -nE '^\+.*V\.(push_back|emplace_back|insert|resize|assign|pop_back)\(' pr.diff` the growth calls. Keep only triples on one container inside one function (confirm with the HEAD-line mapping). `.data()` on a std::array or std::span never counts. A named constant as the reserve argument does not trigger.
6. `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<ref line>,<last use>p' | grep -n -E 'V\.(push_back|emplace_back|insert|resize|assign|pop_back)\(|continue;|break;|return'`. Record what bounds the pushes (tree depth, shard size, an assert); if not written next to the reserve, the finding is the question. For each growth call follow every path to the next read of the reference; a read reached without `continue`, `break` or `return` upgrades the question to a defect. After `pop_back()` every later use must re-take `back()`.

Arm C (scratch handed to a SIMD consumer):
7. `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -nE '^\+.*(std::array<(bf16|float|uint8_t|__m256i|__m512i), *[A-Za-z_0-9]+>|^\+\s*(bf16|float|uint8_t) [a-z_]+\[)' | grep -v alignas` (the comma excludes pointer-element tables such as `std::array<uint8_t const*, N>`; `-- h src` keeps test-local arrays out, they are read in step 10).
8. Consumers: the direct callee; for a `std::function` member `git -C WT grep -n '<member> =' HEAD -- h src t` and the production call inside each lambda. Resolve to one overload: take the pointer type of the callback's destination parameter and keep the overload of the production call whose last parameter has that type (`git -C WT show HEAD:<consumer file> | grep -n '<fn>('`, read each signature). Bound the grep to that body: `START=<signature line>; END=$(awk -v s=$START 'NR>s && /^}/ {print NR; exit}' <file>); sed -n "${START},${END}p" <file> | grep -n -E '_mm256_store_si256|_mm256_load_si256|_mm512_(store|load)_(si512|ps|epi)|_mm256_store_ps|_mm512_stream'`, adding START-1 to each hit. A whole-file grep is not a result (kv_cache.hpp has 57 intrinsic lines). Needed alignment: 32 bytes for `_mm256_*` aligned forms, 64 for `_mm512_*`.
9. Declared alignment: `alignas(N)` on the line; otherwise open the element type's definition (`git -C WT grep -n -E '^(struct|class) <T>\b' HEAD -- h`) and take its alignas if present, else the alignment of its single member (`__bf16`, `uint16_t` 2 bytes, `float` 4); for `bf16` this is h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp:12-13 `struct bf16 { __bf16 content; }`, 2 bytes. Heap buffers: the allocator argument. Sibling: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n alignas`; `git -C WT grep -n 'HWCACHEBLOCK_ALIGN_BYTES =' HEAD -- h/pos/config.hpp` gives the constant.
10. Test reach: `git -C WT grep -n -E '<consumer>\(|<production fn>\(' HEAD -- t/` and read whether the test's callback calls the real consumer or copies with `std::copy_n`.
11. Runtime proof, two forms. (a) Needs no tron build: a 15-line file that declares an `alignas(64)` array, passes `array + 8` (16 bytes past the boundary) to a `__attribute__((noinline))` function that executes the consumer's exact store intrinsic; build with `g++ -O1 -mavx2 -fsanitize=alignment -fno-sanitize-recover=alignment` (`-mavx512f` for `_mm512_*`); run on any host with the instruction set (`grep -o -m1 avx2 /proc/cpuinfo`). "store to misaligned address ... requires 32 byte alignment" is the proof; the aligned pointer must print ok. (b) Needs the tron build: compile the declaring function with `-S` and read the stack offset. If neither runs, write `Insufficient data: not compiled` and say which was blocked. An optimizing compiler can fuse the store into an unaligned form, so a green normal build is not proof.

On PR 4128, Arm C at 97de6ee02c (in WT, BASE 130ad3a652): step 7 gives 1 hit, src/tron/gof.cpp:436 `std::array<std::array<bf16, HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE>, HW_MAX_KV_HEADS> v_scratch;` (the draft regex without the comma gave 3: also gof.cpp:270 `qdatas` pointer table and t/t_phase1_integration.cpp:832); :445 passes `v_scratch[h].data()` to get_v_head, which calls `page.v_head_into_fn(layer, head, scratch)` at :34-35; member h/tron/gof.hpp:76; one production assignment h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2519 whose lambda calls `pg_ptr->get_v(slot, kv_head, off, dest)` with `bf16* dest`; the bf16* overload h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2096-2120 stores with `_mm256_store_si256` at :2109 and :2117 (32 bytes); declared alignment 2 bytes (bf16.hpp:12-13); sibling alignas(HWCACHEBLOCK_ALIGN_BYTES) at gof.cpp:371, constant 64 at h/pos/config.hpp:120; only test callback t/t_phase1_integration.cpp:945-951 is `std::copy_n`; standalone UBSan reproducer fails at +16 bytes and passes aligned (Wade: 'misaligned by 16 bytes'). Fix at 7f80aa17da gof.cpp:417-419 plus t/t_llama_unit.cpp:994-1017 (REQUIRE `dest % HWCACHEBLOCK_ALIGN_BYTES == 0`, then the real `page->get_v`). Arm A at 442ed0dd1a (not in WT; gh api contents): h/tron/gof.hpp:267-281 gof_dma_batch; src/tron/gof.cpp:40-42 `~gof_dma_batch() { if (data) dma_deallocate(data, size); }` unconditional, :44-52 complete() decrements pins only, :54-58 abandon() nulls `data`; src/pos/dma_tracker.cpp:152-166 clear() calls `abandon()` then `q.pop()` without waiting; :57-61 `~dma_tracker` erases itself from the registry and does NOT call clear(), so a tracker destroyed with queued records reaches the batch destructor and frees under live DMA = the forwarded item; pinned assert 0 hits. 97de6ee02c is not an ancestor of 7f80aa17da; its twin fd9fa17f9d (same subject, 2026-09-03) is; at both, clear() :159-190 waits (`hwcacheblock::wait` :180, `complete()` :188) and `~dma_tracker` :58-68 calls clear() at :67, so Arm A does not fire there (the author chose wait-in-clear, not abandon-in-destructor; `~gof_dma_batch` :278-280 still frees unconditionally). Arm A narrowed regex on the 97de diff: 15 hits (draft regex 24). Arm B on PR 2499 at 54a6fd7d1c (BASE = merge-base with origin/main): step 5 gives `stk.reserve(64)` (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1395), references :1403 `frame_t& f = stk.back();` and :1956 `auto& p = stk.back();`, 2 growth calls on stk; step 6: push :1850 -> `pushed_child = true` :1853 -> `break` :1854 -> `continue` :1858, pop :1953 then re-take :1956, so no dangling read; the finding is the question (no bound written next to the reserve). Head 269418ce4d:1395 `stk.reserve(1024);` (214156bd44, after the approval), container unchanged. Arm B on PR 4128: 0 literal reserves, no finding.
